# q317 multiplicity-one descendant semantic closure

**Status:** exact finite source-recursion closure following the q317 square-lift breakout  
**Date:** 2026-08-16  
**Verifier:** `verify_q317_multiplicity_one_descendant_closure.py`  
**Depends on:** `Q317-SQUARE-LIFT-CHARACTER-BREAKOUT.md`, `Q13-Q167-SOURCE-SEMANTIC-SPLIT.md`, the Jacobi-saturation lemma, and h169 class-seed/source data.  
**Claim boundary:** this theorem closes the multiplicity-one Jacobi-saturation descendants generated by the q317 exponent-two branches. Higher q-adic valuations, multiple routed factors, and exact-state promotion remain live. This is not a termination theorem or Erdős–Straus proof.

## 1. Starting graph

The landed q317 square-lift theorem gives

```text
q317^2
  +-- k39 miss  -> q13 positive
  `-- k167 miss -> q167 positive.
```

The landed semantic-split theorem then gives

```text
q13  : no new multiplicity-one character source
q167 : k71 miss -> q71 positive
       k111 miss -> q37 positive.
```

The only unresolved multiplicity-one descendants are therefore

```text
q37
q71.
```

## 2. Complete q71 multiplicity-one closure

For one routed copy of q71, the seed

```text
S71(k)=lcm(gcd(210,(169+k)/4),71)
```

has at most five distinct prime factors. Therefore any Jacobi saturation must satisfy

```text
phi(k)<=486,
k<=236196.
```

The complete finite q71 route closure has

```text
76 compatible low-totient route shifts
```

and exactly four saturations:

```text
k=7
k=11
k=23
k=31.
```

Every saturated miss is character-idempotent:

```text
k7  -> (7/p)=+1   already controlled
k11 -> (11/p)=+1  already controlled
k23 -> (23/p)=+1  already controlled
k31 -> (31/p)=+1  already controlled.
```

Thus q71 is a multiplicity-one semantic sink:

```text
q71 -> no new fixed positive character.
```

A direct hit at any of the four destinations remains constructive.

## 3. Complete q37 multiplicity-one closure

For one routed copy of q37 the same rigorous bound applies.

The complete finite q37 route closure has

```text
77 compatible low-totient route shifts
```

and exactly five saturations:

```text
k=3
k=7
k=11
k=27
k=71.
```

The first four are miss-side idempotent:

```text
k3  -> (3/p)=+1   hard-class character
k7  -> (7/p)=+1   already controlled
k11 -> (11/p)=+1  already controlled
k27 -> (27/p)=+1  equivalent to the already-controlled q3 character.
```

The only new output is k71:

```text
k71 hit
or
k71 miss -> (71/p)=+1.
```

Therefore

```text
q37 -> q71
```

is the only multiplicity-one source-generation edge from q37.

Since q71 is a sink, the q37 branch closes after one additional source-generation step.

## 4. Exact descendant graph

Combining the landed q13/q167 theorem with the new q37/q71 closures gives the complete multiplicity-one descendant graph rooted at the q317 square lift:

```text
                 q13
                 [sink]
                /
q317^2 --------<
                \
                 q167
                 /  \
               q71  q37
               [sink] \
                       q71
                       [sink]
```

Equivalently, the only source-generation edges are

```text
q317^2 -> q13
q317^2 -> q167
q167    -> q71
q167    -> q37
q37     -> q71.
```

There are no multiplicity-one source-generation edges leaving q13 or q71.

The set of new descendant character primes is finite:

```text
{13,167,37,71}.
```

## 5. Why this is stronger than a census

Each source closure is exhaustive under a rigorous cardinality bound.

For a multiplicity-one routed source q, the destination seed has at most five distinct prime factors, so

```text
#Div(S^2)<=243.
```

Jacobi saturation therefore requires

```text
phi(k)<=486,
```

and odd admissible k satisfies

```text
k<=486^2=236196.
```

The verifier exhausts the complete bounded route spaces for q37 and q71 and composes them with the already-landed complete q13/q167 closures.

So the graph closure is theorem-backed, not an empirical cutoff in source size or destination depth.

## 6. Machine consequence

The candidate framework may add a multiplicity-one recursion rule:

```text
DESCENDANTS(q317^2) = {q13,q167,q37,q71}

q13  -> CHARACTER_IDEMPOTENT + phase contraction already recorded
q71  -> CHARACTER_IDEMPOTENT
q37  -> q71
q167 -> {q37,q71}
```

Hence an algorithm must not keep recursively expanding multiplicity-one Jacobi character routes from this family after q71. The exact graph is closed.

Continued progress must come from at least one of:

```text
higher valuation,
multiple routed factors,
new affine/support transfer,
exact-state promotion,
incoming repulsion,
direct signed-box geometry.
```

This deletes an infinite-looking but actually finite recursion pattern from the scheduler.

## 7. Candidate progress semantics

This graph suggests a useful distinction between **proof-resource growth** and **semantic closure**.

For this family:

```text
SOURCE_GENERATION can occur,
but multiplicity-one SOURCE_GENERATION_DEPTH is bounded by 2 after q317^2.
```

That depth is a proved local bound for this descendant graph. It is not a global decomposition ordinal.

The machine may safely record

```text
MULT1_DESCENDANT_CLOSED = true
```

once a branch reaches q13 or q71 without a terminal hit.

It may not infer global failure or prune higher-valuation states.

## 8. Bryan Entanglement Cross boundary

The exact graph gives a natural observational history:

```text
up (+/-): q317 square valuation opens new source branches
right (+): q13/q167 are generated
right (+): q167 can generate q37/q71
right (+): q37 can generate q71
left/down: multiplicity-one recursion closes at q13/q71
```

BEC/BREC describes the transition shape only. The finite closure and saturation identities are proof-bearing.

## 9. Next target

The most valuable next question is now valuation-sensitive:

> Do q13 or q71 cease to be semantic sinks at exponent two, as q317 did?

If both remain closed for all valuation layers under a finite theorem, that would strengthen the local closure dramatically. If either breaks out, its first productive lift becomes the next exact transition in the machine.
